abstract.p: Disclosed are flavor enhancing oils comprising at least one edible liquid oil and at least one water soluble flavor enhancer. The water soluble flavor enhancer is uniformly dispersed throughout the edible liquid oil. Delivery of water soluble flavor enhancers via a stable fat or oil base allows higher temperatures to be obtained during cooking, leading to the formation of enhanced flavors.

Ces huiles renforçatrices d'arôme renferment au moins une huile liquide comestible et au moins un renforçateur d'arôme hydrosoluble. Ce dernier est uniformément dispersé dans l'huile liquide comestible. La libération de renforçateurs d'arôme hydrosolubles présents dans une matière grasse ou une huile stable autorise une cuisson à des températures plus élevées, ce qui se solde par la formation d'arômes plus prononcés.

description.p: FLAVOR ENHANCING OILS
FIELD OF THE INVENTION
The present invention relates to oils such as cooking oil, cooking spray, and shortening compositions which comprise an effective amount of a water soluble flavor enhancer
BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

Flavor enhancers are substances which have little flavor themselves, but which "enhance" or "intensify" the flavor of the foods to which they are added The flavor display effected by flavor enhancers is often characterized as "savory" or "full-bodied," and has been termed "umami" by the Japanese

Water soluble flavor enhancers, such as nucleotide and ammo acid flavor enhancers, are among the most common "umani" flavor enhancers. They are commonly available m the form of powders which can be solubilized in food substances havmg an aqueous phase. In the case of soups, for example, the incorporation of water soluble flavor enhancers is relatively simple, as the flavor enhancers are readily dissolved and unifoimly dispersed throughout the soup's aqueous phase.

At relatively high cooking temperatures, water soluble flavor enhancers can decompose into products which provide even more enhanced flavor displays. Delivery of these flavor enhancers via aqueous phase, however, limits the amount of such flavor enhancement that can be provided When in aqueous phase, the highest temperature that can typically be reached during cooking is about 100°C (the boiling point of water) Most cooking systems utilizing heated fats or oils, however, operate at temperatures of from about 200°F to about 500°F For example, gπddling operations utilize temperatures as high as about 400°F. In certain operations, such as deep fat frying, temperatures as high as about 400°F and above are employed. However, frying oils and gnllmg fats contain no aqueous phase in which to uniformly disperse these flavor enhancers. Thus, the delivery of water soluble flavor enhancers via frying and gnllmg operations, and the enhanced flavor displays obtamed at higher cooking temperatures, have not been practical.

Accordingly, in order to take full advantage of the flavor benefits that water soluble flavor enhancers can deliver, it would be desirable to provide a cooking oil compnsing uniformly dispersed, water soluble flavor enhancers.
SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION
The present mvention provides a cooking oil compnsing uniformly dispersed, water soluble flavor enhancers This flavor enhancing oil comprises
(a) at least one edible liquid oil; and

(b) a flavor enhancing amount of at least one water soluble flavor enhancer
The edible liquid oil can be any suitable edible fat or oil which is solid, plastic, or fluid at room temperature, and quifiable (1 e liquid) at room temperature or upon heating Preferred flavor enhancers include ammo acid flavor enhancers, such as monosodium glutamate (MSG), and nucleotide flavor enhancers, such as disodium guanylate and disolium mosmate The water soluble flavor enhancers are included in the edible liquid oil in a flavor enhancing amount Typically, the water soluble flavor enhancers can be included m the edible liquid oil at a level of up to about 20%, more particularly up to about 15%, still more particularly up to about 10%, in one embodiment between about 0 01% to about 7%, more preferably between about 0 01% to about 4%, and still more preferably from about 0.01% to about 2% The flavor enhancing oil can also contain optional ingredients such as an oxoacid

The result of preparing foods usmg these blends is an enhancement of the natural, inherent flavor of the food without the necessity of addmg a dominant flavormg, which can be the case with conventional butter flavored sprays and spice flavored cooking oils Accordmgly, the compositions of the present invention can be used to bring out the natural flavor of food, or alternatively, can be used with other flavor mgredients to provide specific desired flavormg (e.g., butter, olive oil, fπed flavor notes, spicy, tangy, lemon, garlic, herb ).

The food preparation composition is not only useful as a replacement for salad and cookmg oils, but it can also be used to formulate other edible fat products such as, but not limited to, shortening, peanut butter, peanut spread, mayonnaise, sauces, gravies, margarine, health bars, snacks, beverages, ice cream, yogurt, cake mix, frostmg, donuts, baked goods (e.g , breads and muffins), cheese, and cheese spreads.

The food preparation composition can be used in all applications that call for salad and cookmg oil such as stove top cookmg (pan frying, sauteing stir frying etc ), baking, and as an ingredient m recipes that are not cooked (salad dressing, mayonnaise).
The invention delivers the above benefits in an oil based form which allows for increased cook temperatures and the resultant mcreased formation of flavor compounds during cookmg.
DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION DEFINITIONS

As used herein, all percentages (%) are by weight, unless otherwise mdicated. As used herein, "flavor enhancer" refers to a substance which has little flavor itself, but when added to food, has the property of enhancing or intensifying the flavor of the food. Flavor enhancers mclude, but are not limited to, flavor precursors, flavor potentiators, reaction flavors, and agents that suppress or mask undesirable flavors.

As used herem, the term "food preparation composition" refers to compositions useful in preparmg cooked and un-cooked foods, including but not limited to cookmg oils, cookmg sprays, shortenings, sauces, seasoning compositions, salad dressings, and marinades.
As used herein, the term "edible liquid oil" broadly includes all those edible fats or oils which are solid, plastic, or fluid (1 e , liquid) at room temperature (about 70CF) Generally, the fat must be liquifiable at room temperature or upon heating Suitable fats which are solid or plastic at room temperature generally melt or liquefy at those temperatures encountered m cook g operations. Also included by the term are suitable fat and oil substitutes

As used herein, the term "oil" refers in general to pourable (at room temperature) edible oils derived from animals or plants, including but not limited to fish oils, liquefied animal fats, and vegetable oils, including but not limited to corn, coconut, soybean, olive, cottonseed, safflower oil, sunflower oil, canola, peanut oil, and combmations thereof (hydrogenated, non-hydrogenated, and partially hydrogenated oil). The oil can comprise a liquid, or a combmation of liquid and solid particles (e.g., fat particles in a liquid base) In addition, the term "oil" includes fat substitutes, which can be used alternatively or m combmation with animal and/or plant oils A suitable fat substitute is sucrose polyester, such as is available from the Procter & Gamble Co. under the trade name OLEAN® The following U.S. Patents disclose fat substitutes, and are incorporated herem by reference US 4,880,657 issued November 14, 1989; US 4,960,602 issued October 2, 1990, US 4,835,001 issued May 30, 1989; US 5,422,131 issued January 2, 1996. Other suitable fat substitutes mclude SALATRIM® brand product from Nabisco and various alkoxylated polyols such as those described in the following U S. Patents incorporated herem by reference- 4,983,329; 5,175,323; 5,288,884; 5,298,637, 5,362,894; 5,387,429; 5,446,843; 5,589,217, 5,597,605, 5,603,978; and 5,641,534. As used herem, the term "diglyceπde" refers to esters of glycerol and fatty acids m which any two of the hydroxyl groups of the glycerol have been esteπfied with fatty acids. The fatty acids may be the same or different.

As used herem, the term "dairy diglyceπde" refers to the diglyceπde fraction resulting from the enzymatic or chemical hydrolysis of a dairy food such as milk, cream, butter or cheese. As used herem the terms "oxoacid" and "alpha keto acid" refer to a compound with the general structure:

As used herein, "polyglycerol esters" are homologues of glyceπdes

As used herem, the term "lecithin" is a generic name for a class of compounds which are mixed esters of glycerol and choline with fatty acids and phosphoric acid as well as the derivatives thereof The term 'lecithin" includes conventional lecithins acylated (included acetylated) lecithins, and other suitable lecithin or lecithin-like compounds such as de-oiled lecithin, lysolecithins, phosphatidic acid and its salts, lysophosphatidic acid and its salts, and mixtures thereof
As used herem, the term "nucleotide flavor enhancer" includes 5'-πbonucleotιdes and their corresponding derivatives, such as salts thereof
THE FLAVOR ENHANCING OIL
The flavor enhancing oil of the present invention comprises (a) at least one edible liquid oil, and (b) a flavor enhancing amount of at least one water soluble flavor enhancer
A Edible Liquid Oil

The composition of the present mvention can include an oil base compnsing tnglycendes, such as vegetable oil Alternatively, the composition can have a base compnsmg a fat substitute, such as a polyol polyester (e g sucrose polyester such as olestra ), or a combination of tπglyceπde oil and polyol polyester

In one embodiment of the present invention, the edible liquid oil can compnse between about 35% and about 99% of the flavor enhancing oil Alternatively, or m combination with the oil, a fat substitute can be used in the base A suitable fat substitute is sucrose polyester, such as is available from the Procter & Gamble Co under the trade name OLEAN® The following U S Patents disclose fat substitutes, and are incorporated herein by reference 4,880,657 issued November 14, 1989, 4,960,602 issued October 2, 1990, 4,835,001 issued May 30, 1989, and 5,422,131 issued January 2, 1996 Other suitable fat substitutes include SALATRIM® brand product from Nabisco and vanous alkoxylated polyols such as those descnbed m the following U S Patents incorporated herem by reference 4,983,329, 5, 175,323, 5,288,884, 5,298,637, 5,362,894, 5,387,429, 5,446,843, 5,589,217, 5,597,605, 5,603,978, and 5,641,534

A preferred embodiment utilizes a blend of liquid sucrose polyester and a structured tnglycende that is soluble in liquid sucrose polyester such as a tnglycende contammg two liquid fatty acid chams (C2 to CIO saturated fatty acid chams or C16-C22 mono- or polyunsaturated chainlengths) and one solid fatty acid chains (C18-C24 saturated fatty acid chainlengths) as described in US 5,419,925, Seiden, issued May 5, 1995 (equivalent to European Patent No 390,410 B l ) and incorporated herem by reference In vivo polysis of the structured tnglycende hydrolyzes the fatty acid moieties from the 1 and 3 positions on the tnglycende leavmg 2-monoglycendes The resultmg behenic acid, calcium salts of behenic acid and 2-

be delivered m the form of a shortening A typical shortening contains liquid tnglycende oil, an intermediate meltmg fraction tnglycende (IMF), a small amount of hardstock tπglyceπde and an emulsifier such as a monoglycende The compositions of the present mvention can replace all or part of the liquid tnglycende oil and some of the intermediate melting fraction tnglycende and hardstock tnglycende
A Flavor Enhancer

The flavor enhancing oil compnses a flavor enhancer that accentuates the cooked flavor of the food prepared therewith The flavor enhancer can be selected from nucleotide flavor enhancers such as 5'- IMP (5'-ιnosιnιc acid) and 5'-GMP (5'-guanylιc acid), or their coπesponding salts such as disodium guanylate, disodium mosmate, dipotassium guanylate, dipotassium mosmate, and mixtures thereof Especially preferred are mixtures wherem the ratio of disodium guanylate to disodium mosmate is
between about 1 0 to about 0 1 , and more preferably from about 1 0 to about 0 5 0 5 A suitable 0 5 0 5 combination of disodium guanylate and disodium mosmate is commercially available from the Takeda Company, under the Ribotide® brand name

Other suitable flavor enhancers include ammo acid flavor enhancers such as monosodium glutamate (MSG), monopotassium glutamate, and mixtures thereof Additional suitable flavor enhancers include, but are not limited to, maltol, ethyl maltol, nucleotide-containing compositions denved from shiitake or other suitable mushrooms, disodium succmate (SSA), suitable cultured whey protems such as Flavor Whey (available from the PTX Corporation), and mixtures thereof.

Suitable yeast extracts, such as autolyzed yeast extracts (AYE), can also be used Prefened yeast extracts are naturally nch m 5'-nucleotιdes and include Yeast Extract 2006 from the BioSprmger Company and Flavor Mate 950, Flavor Mate 960, and Flavor Mate 945, all available from Red Star BioProducts Suitable carbohydrate decomposition products, such as Furaneol®, available from the Firmenich company, can also be used
An especially preferred flavor enhancer compπses a combmation of MSG with a nucleotide flavor enhancer such as disodium guanylate, disodium mosmate, or mixtures thereof.

The flavor enhancing oil compnses a flavor enhancing amount of at least one water soluble flavor enhancer The flavor enhancing oil can compnse up to about 20% flavor enhancer, more particularly up to about 15%>, still more particularly up to about 10%, in one embodiment between about 0.01% to about 7%, more preferably between about 0.01% to about 4% flavor enhancer, and still more preferably from about 0 01% to about 2% flavor enhancer.
B Optional Ingredients
1 Anti-Stick Agent

The food preparation composition of the present mvention can comprise an anti-stick agent, such as lecithm or modified lecithm (such as acetylated lecithin) for reducing the tendency of food to adhere to cookmg utensils, and to provide browning. Without bemg limited by theory, it is believed that lecithm, m the appropnate amount, can act synergistically with the oxoacids and flavor enhancer to deliver an unproved brown/fried color and flavor to cooked foods.

The composition can compnse up to about 20% lecithm, more particularly up to about 15% lecithm, still more particularly up to about 10% lecithm, and m one embodiment between about 0.5% and about 7% lecithm, more preferably between about 0 5% and about 4% lecithm A suitable lecithm is commercially available from the Central Soya Co , as CENTROPHASE® 152 brand A suitable acylated lecithm is the acetylated lecithm commercially available from the Central Soya Co. as CENTROPHASE® HR brand. Other suitable lecithm or lecithin-like compounds which can be used mclude de-oiled lecithm, lysolecithins, phosphatidic acid and its salts, and lysophosphatidic acid and its salts.
The use of a silica compound, such as silicon dioxide, also imparts anti-stick properties to the food preparation composition Especially prefeπed is the used of lecithin in combination with silicon dioxide for producing the desired anti-stick effects Fumed silica is a preferred form of silicon dioxide A suitable fumed silica is commercially available from Degussa, Inc . under the trade name Aerosil® 380 The composition can comprise up to about 10%), preferably up to about 5%, more preferably up to about 3%, and most preferably up to about 2%, of a silica compound or mixtures thereof
2 Mouthfeel Agent

The flavor enhancing oil of the present invention can compnse a mouthfeel agent for increasmg the actual or perceived lubπsciousness of the food cooked with the composition In one embodiment of the present mvention, the composition compnses diglycende, oxoacids, or combinations thereof for providmg a lubπcious mouthfeel

The composition can compnse between about 0 0005%) to about 2% diglycende (This amount of diglycende is m addition to that which may compnse the edible liquid oil ) Suitable diglycendes include those from edible plant or animal precursors A preferred diglyceπde compnses dairy diglycende The composition can compnse between about 0 000005%) and about 0 005%) by weight oxoacids The oxoacid can comprise oxopropanoic acid, oxobutanoic acid, oxopentanoic acid, oxohexanoic acid, oxoheptanoic acid, or mixtures thereof The oxoacid can also compnse an oxoacid selected from the group consisting of glyoxihc acid, 2-oxopropanoιc acid, 2 oxobutanoic acid, 3-methyl-2- oxobutanoic acid, 3-methyl-2-oxo-pentanoιc acid, 4-methyl-2-oxo-pentanoιc acid, 3-hydroxy-2-oxo- propanoic acid, 3-hydroxy-2-oxobutanoιc acid, oxolacetic acid, 2-oxo-glutanc acid, 2-oxo-3- phenylpropanoic acid, 3-(4-hydroxyphenyl)-2-oxopropanoιc acid, 2-oxo-lH-ιndol-3-propanoιc acid, 4- (methylthιo)-2-oxo-pentanoιc acid, 6-amιno-2-oxo-hexanoιc acid, 3-mercapto-2-oxo-propanoιc acid, 3- methyl-2-oxo-hexanoιc acid, 3-methyl-2-oxo-heptanoιc acid, and mixtures thereof A suitable combmation of dairy diglycende and oxoacid havmg a butter flavor is available from the Firmenich Company of Geneva, Switzerland
3 Anti-Foaming Agents

The food preparation composition can compnse sihcone polymer to reduce the foaming of the composition during cookmg The sihcone polymer is present at such as level as to have no detectable taste or aroma or flavor The food preparation composition can compnse from about 1 ppm to about 1000 ppm, preferably from about 4 ppm to about 200 ppm, and more preferably about 10 ppm, sihcone polymer

A preferred sihcone polymer is polydimethylsiloxane Preferably, the polydimethylsiloxane has a viscosity of from about 200 to about 1200 centistokes at 25°C, more preferably from about 300 to about 1,050 centistokes at 25°C, and most preferably about 350 centistokes at 25°C A particularly suitable
commercially available polydimethylsiloxane is DowS 200 Fluid brand, available from Dow Chemical Company

The use of a silica compound, such as silicon dioxide, also imparts anti-foam properties to the food preparation composition Especially prefeπed is the use of sihcone polymer in combination with silicon dioxide for producing the desired anti-foam effects Fumed silica is a prefened form of silicon dioxide. A suitable fumed silica is commercially available from Degussa, Inc., under the trade name Aerosil® 380 The composition can comprise up to about 10%, preferably up to about 5%, more preferably up to about 3%, and most preferably up to about 2%, of a silica compound or mixtures thereof
4 Other Ingredients Additional flavor mgredients and masking agents can be mcluded m the flavor enhancing oil.

Such additional flavor and masking agents mclude, but are not limited to, terpene hydrocarbons and sunflower oil Terpene hydrocarbons may be predominantly pure compounds, such as d-lunonene; or byproducts of the citrus processing industry, such as cold pressed citrus oils (e.g., lemon, lime, orange, grapefruit, tangerme), citrus essence, or phase oils, or may be terpene mixtures separated from peel or essence oils by distillation or extraction. Natural and artificial meat flavors can also be used.

The compositions of the present mvention can also mclude mgredients mcludmg, but not limited to, antioxidants, chelatmg agents, ammo acids (e.g. alpha ammo acids such as cysteme, methiomne, lysine, and glycine), artificial and natural sweeteners mcludmg sugar (e.g., sucrose, fructose, xylose), vitamins (e.g., Vitamins A, C, E, and the B vitamins), and other nutnents and minerals. For example, the compositions of the present mvention can mclude flavor precursors such as alpha-ammo acids, protem hydrolysates, yeast autolysates, reducing compounds, vitamins, and mixtures thereof.

The compositions of the present mvention can mclude one or more emulsifiers mcludmg, but not limited to, monoglycendes, diglycerol oleate, diglcerol noleate, and/or coemulsifiers and cosolvents (e.g., ethanol). The compositions may also mclude an ingredient such as enzyme modified egg yolk for use in an oil m water emulsion.

The food preparation compositions of the present mvention, according to one embodiment, can have a pH which is between about 4 and about 7, and more particularly between about 5 and about 6. Without bemg limited by theory, it is believed that such a pH range can be desirable to control browning of food prepared with the flavor enhancing oils of the present mvention. The pH of the food preparation composition can be controlled by the addition of a suitable edible acid, such as citnc acid.
